subject: Using Facets to Show Axis Breaks?

messages.author: 1e82ea932416652e
messages.subject: Using Facets to Show Axis Breaks?
parts:
As an exercise, I am attempting to create some example graphs using R
that show different ways to handle highly skewed data. The basic
approaches include plotting the logarithm of the skewed values, or
using some version of an axis break. Cleveland gives an example in
“The Elements of Graphing Data,” pp 103 – 104, where he uses a
completely separate panel for each scale break, but maintains the
continuity of the non-skewed axis. I've been able to reproduce
something comparable using Lattice: http://yfrog.com/b9rplot2p.

I'm struggling with how to reproduce this, or its equivalent, with
ggplot2.

The code to produce the plot using lattice is below. Any suggestions
for how to do something similar with ggplot2 is appreciated.

library(lattice)
month <- c("Feb 09", "Mar 09", "Apr 09", "May 09", "Jun 09", "Jul 09",
"Aug 09", "Sep 09", "Oct 09", "Nov 09", "Dec 09", "Jan 10", "Feb 10")
sales <- c(200,300,200,300,200,300,350,400,450,1200,100000,85000,450)
SalesRange <- shingle(sales, intervals = rbind(c(0, 5000), c(5000,
200000)))
salesdata <- data.frame(month = month, sales = sales, order = c(1:13),
SalesRange = SalesRange)
salesdata$month <- reorder(salesdata$month, rev(salesdata$order))
dotplot(month ~ sales | SalesRange, data = salesdata, strip = FALSE,
layout = c(2, 1), levels.fos = 1:50, scales = list(x = "free"),
between = list(x = 0.5), par.settings = list(layout.widths =
list(panel = c(2, 1))), xlab = "Sales (US$ x 1000)")

Many thanks,

Tom

Here's a start: I don't know off the top of my head (1) how to
suppress the strips; (2) how to manually set the layout widths
(space="free" will keep the x axes on the same scale; doing it this way
divides the x-axis space equally; I don't know how to do anything in
between) (3) tweak the x-axis labels so they are all 'nice'. It does
seem a tiny bit dicey on graphical-presentation grounds to both
introduce an axis break *and* allow the scale to be different in the
different sub-plots ...

library(ggplot2)
salesdata$bigsales <- salesdata$sales>80000
ggplot(salesdata,aes(x=sales,y=month))+geom_point()+
facet_grid(.~bigsales,scales="free_x")+theme_bw()+
xlab("Sales (US$ x 1000)")

messages.subject: Re: Using Facets to Show Axis Breaks?
parts:
Ben,

Thanks for the suggestion; it is a good start. I'll play around and see what I can do with it.

Regarding having an axis break with different scales in the subplots, I think you're probably right. Cleveland does it (pp 105 of The Elements of Graphing Data), but he uses a bar above each sub-plot to indicate the same range, so that it is somewhat clearer that the axis scale has changed, and by how much. As I recall, he also indicates that taking the log of the data is the preferred method, but I find that many audiences struggle with correctly interpreting log scales.

Regards,

Tom
